summary.text: Republican Joe Strada won the open seat for Florida's 11th Congressional District on November 3, 2026, defeating James Pericola, according to unofficial results.
According to his campaign website, he started in the skilled trades and grew a family-owned Central Florida company, Strada Services, and he describes himself as not a career politician.

paragraphs.text: Strada graduated from Lyman High School, according to Ballotpedia, and his campaign website says he took a job as a handyman at a bowling alley while still in high school.

He entered the skilled trades and, according to his campaign website, grew Strada Services from one van into a family-owned company serving communities across the country, which he says created thousands of jobs.

He says he invested in paid training programs so employees could learn a trade while earning pay, which is why workforce development, apprenticeships and career and technical education were central to his campaign.
Ballotpedia lists Strada's profession as business, and he describes himself as a businessman and not a career politician.
He won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary for Florida's 11th District with 33.5% of the vote, ahead of Carey Baker (33.0%), Tim Wilkins, Nizam Razack and Ivette Palomo.
According to his campaign website, he campaigned on immigration enforcement, government accountability, term limits and workforce training.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 52.9% of the vote to James Pericola's 46%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
According to his campaign website, he and his wife raised their family in Central Florida, and he is a father and grandfather.
